_comment: Source of truth for this service's entire RabbitMQ topology (event-contract.md; the draft manifest in kart-platform/docs/services/kart-offer-service/message-bus-manifest.json only sketched the two inbound consumer queues - this file completes it with this service's own publishing topology and CQRS read-model projection queue). Nothing here is hardcoded in C# - RabbitMqTopologyProvisioner declares every exchange/queue/binding/DLQ/retry-tier straight from this file at startup, exactly like kart-identity-service/kart-category-service/kart-delivery-tracking-service. CouponRedeemed/CouponRedemptionVoided/CouponIssued/CouponDeactivated/PriceQuoteIssued/PromotionActivated/PromotionDeactivated are all published via this service's own EF Core/PostgreSQL transactional outbox (OutboxRelayHostedService), which retries indefinitely until RabbitMQ is reachable rather than dead-lettering - so, per the same convention used across services, published events appear only in publishedEvents, never with a DLQ of their own. offer.read-model-projection.queue is this service's own internal async pipeline: it self-consumes every event this service just published on offer.exchange to keep the MongoDB denormalized read models (CQRS query side) in sync with the PostgreSQL write side - the same 'self-consumed event' shape kart-delivery-tracking-service uses for its own internal ingestion pipeline, applied here to CQRS projection instead.
